subject: Novalex: tail latency & traffic matrix (hosted vs incumbent) — follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@novalex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Novalex: tail latency & traffic matrix (hosted vs incumbent) — follow-up

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next items we discussed so we can qualify p95/p99 E2E latency for Hosted vs your incumbent provider.

Recap (short):
- Goal: determine whether Redwood Hosted can meet Novalex's p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 450ms SLA for conversational inference across your production traffic mix.
- Primary constraints: streaming latency for real-time agents, concurrency spikes during peak (market open), and multi-tenant batching behavior.
- Scope: end-to-end (client SDK -> Redwood Hosted -> model -> response streaming), including edge network and our client-side SDK buffering.

Requested artifacts / asks (action items):
1) Traffic matrix CSV (attached template) with typical RPS, payload size distribution, streaming vs non-streaming percentage, and concurrency per-minute for peak window (you mentioned 30–45 minute surges).
2) Representative sample prompt sizes (tokens) and average generated token counts for each endpoint (chat vs single-turn generate).
3) Any egress/networking constraints (IP allowlists, regional routing) and test accounts we can use to run a parallel hosted trial.

What we'll deliver after we get the matrix:
- A short runbook mapping your traffic buckets to Redwood test harness scenarios.
- An estimate of expected p95/p99 tail based on our serving profile + a recommended PoC configuration (streaming concurrency limits, batch target, quantization level).
- A one-week hosted PoC plan (traffic replay or live traffic mirror) with acceptance criteria.

Attachments: novalex_traffic_matrix_sample.csv (template), redwood_hosted-sla-questions.pdf (details on what we measure).

Timing: if you can send the matrix by EOD Wed PST we can turn around the traffic-to-scenario mapping by Fri COB and propose a PoC start next week.

Thanks —Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132
From: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@novalex.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novalex Platform Team <novalex-support@novalex.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Novalex: tail latency & traffic matrix (hosted vs incumbent) — follow-up

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. I attached a filled-in CSV with our high-level traffic buckets. A couple of clarifications inline: 

- Peak windows: we have two (US market open 09:30–10:15 ET, and EU midday 13:00–14:00 ET). Peak per-instance concurrency is typically 320–420 concurrent sessions; sustained RPS during peak ~ 1.8k with spikes to ~2.6k lasting ~2–5 minutes.
- Streaming: ~27% of requests use streaming (agent UI), but streaming sessions are long-running; most streaming sends small incremental tokens every 200–400ms.
- Token counts: median prompt ~ 85 tokens, median generated ~ 42 tokens; long-tail prompts (10%) are 600+ tokens and generate up to 400 tokens.
- Incumbent baseline: our provider reports p95=135ms, p99=520ms (measured client-side). We suspect network buffering and SDK batching account for some of the delta.

Attachments: novalex_traffic_matrix_filled.csv (we included a sheet called "peak_buckets"), a short dump of sample traces (sanitized) in the Drive link below.

Questions:
1) For streaming sessions, can Redwood surface partial tokens to the client within 60–80ms from model token emission? We need to understand cumulative client-to-client latency.
2) How do you recommend configuring batching thresholds during short spikes so that tail doesn't inflate?

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bNOVA-sample-traces (sanitized).

Best,
Maria Ortega
Head of Platform Engineering | Novalex
maria.ortega@novalex.com

Forwarding Maria's response and the filled matrix. TL;DR: bigger concurrency spikes (up to ~420), streaming is 27% with small frequent partial tokens, and they have a long tail of very large prompts.

Suggested immediate next steps (assign):
- Ben: can you book a 45-min PoC kickoff with Novalex (Maria + infra) for Wed 11/2 or Thu 11/3? We need to confirm test accounts and whether they prefer live mirror or replay.
- Karthik: please review the attached CSV and produce a short test harness plan that covers: 3 traffic buckets (normal, peak, spike), streaming token cadence, and a plan for client-side SDK latency measurement hooks. Include recommended hosted instance configs (pool size, target batch window, max concurrency per worker).
- Me: I'll draft the PoC acceptance criteria and the measurements we'll report (client p95/p99, server-side tail, token-level latency histogram).

Notes on risk: their measured baseline p99=520ms > our target of 450ms. We need to identify where network/SDK buffering is contributing. A quick experiment: run a mirrored live test traffic for 2 hours during their US peak and compare traces. If they can't mirror, we'll use traffic replay with header-level timing preserved.

Attachments referenced: novalex_traffic_matrix_filled.csv (from Maria).

--
Sean
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novalex: tail latency & traffic matrix (hosted vs incumbent) — follow-up

Got it — I'll schedule the PoC kickoff for Wed 2026-12-02 11:30 PT (Maria confirmed that's workable). Karthik, I'll block 90 minutes after the kickoff for a hands-on run of the traffic replay (we can run both a replay and a small live mirror).

Quick tech notes / plan points:
- For streaming partial latency target: we'll aim for <80ms client-visible partials by setting pipeline flush at token emission and minimizing extra batching on the streaming path; that'll be a config we toggle in PoC.
- For spike behavior: configure an autoscale buffer (burst pool) and apply a conservative max-batch-ms during 2–5 minute spikes to avoid waiting for full batch formation — favor immediate dispatch on heavy concurrency buckets.
- Measurement: we'll instrument both client-side (SDK hooks Maria can add) and our server-side: token emit time, socket flush, and inbound request arrival time. We'll provide per-request histograms to correlate p99 contributors.

I'll update the HubSpot deal and add the PoC agenda.

Ben Carter
